window.head: Window
window.label: When closing the window
window.trayUnavailable: The system tray isn’t available on this computer, so “Hide to system tray” will minimize the window instead.

model.head: Models
model.hint: Connection addresses, protocols, and compatibility switches are under “Edit” on each connection on the Models page; per-model compatibility settings are under “Manage models”.
model.overrideHint: Extra parameters for models, such as context length and image limits. Change addresses, keys, and model lists on the Models page.

engine.head: Chat engine and security
engine.hint: These switches loosen what the assistant can do; leaving them at their defaults is usually best.

own.title: Use my own Pi config
own.confirm: Chat will use the models, keys, and extensions in ~/.pi instead, and RRSS model settings will no longer apply to chat. Turning this off restores the previous setup and keeps your earlier choices.
own.hint: Use the models and keys in ~/.pi.

dev.confirm: The assistant will be able to run commands and read and write files in the working directory. Only turn this on if you understand the consequences.
dev.label: Developer tools
dev.hint: Lets the assistant read and write files and run commands. Off by default.

piPath.label: Pi executable path
piPath.hint: Leave blank to use the version RRSS downloaded, falling back to one installed on the system.
piPath.placeholder: Leave blank to use the downloaded version

engine.settingsOverrideHint: Extra chat engine settings that aren’t in the interface yet. If an entry conflicts with one the app manages, the app’s value wins.

generated.label: Generated config
generated.hint: Parameters and settings used when the chat engine starts; keys are hidden.

override.invalid: {{label}} isn’t a valid JSON object and wasn’t saved. Fix it and try again.

generated.title: Generated config
generated.own: You’re using your own Pi config: models, keys, and extensions come from ~/.pi, and only what RRSS passes in is listed here.
generated.ignored: These override entries are managed by RRSS and were ignored:
generated.unparsable: (Config couldn’t be parsed; file contents not shown)

backup.title: Backup and restore
backup.restarting: Backing up your current data; the app will restart and restore when it’s done…

all.title: Back up all data
all.hint: Articles, feeds, rules, memories, chats, and settings packed into one file.
all.withSecrets: This backup includes keys; keep it safe.

secrets.label: Include keys
secrets.hint: API keys, translation keys, and external tools’ environment variables and request headers. Off by default: a backup on cloud storage or another computer won’t carry your keys, and you can just re-enter them after restoring.

done.note: Media cache and the chat engine program aren’t included; they’ll be downloaded again when needed after restoring.

restore.title: Restore from backup
restore.hint: Replaces all current data; a backup is made automatically first. The app needs to restart.
restore.okLabel: Back up current data and restart to restore

restoreMessage.replace: · All current data will be replaced by this backup.
restoreMessage.autoBackup: · Current data is backed up automatically first (without keys); you’ll need to re-enter keys after restoring from that automatic backup.

auto.title: Automatic backups
auto.hint: Saved in the backups folder in the data directory; only the 5 most recent are kept. A backup is always made before a database upgrade. Automatic backups never include keys.

prefs.title: Export preferences only
prefs.hint: Move just your preferences to another computer, without articles. No keys. Export feeds with OPML on the Feeds page. Import merges, so nothing already there is duplicated.

err.restore: Couldn’t prepare the restore; no data was changed:
err.schedule: Couldn’t save the automatic backup schedule:

format.createdNoSecrets: No keys; re-enter them after restoring
format.restoreNoSecrets: No keys; re-enter API keys and external tool variables after restoring
format.restoreKept: , and files from the backup remain in the {{dir}} folder

kinds.before_prune: Automatic backup before old articles were cleaned up

messages.prefs_empty: The file has nothing to import.
messages.restore_exit_timeout: Couldn’t restore from {{name}}; no data was changed: the previous RRSS run didn’t exit within {{seconds}} seconds, so no files were replaced. Close all RRSS windows and try restoring again
messages.restore_staging_incomplete: Couldn’t restore from {{name}}; no data was changed: the staged backup is incomplete
messages.restore_rolled_back: Couldn’t restore from {{name}}; no data was changed.
messages.restore_partial: Couldn’t restore from {{name}}, and some files couldn’t be moved back. Your original data is in the {{old}} folder in the data directory{{kept}}. Quit RRSS, move those files back into the data directory, and then open the app; don’t delete these folders.

skip.rule_scope_missing: Rule {{rule}}: limited to {{scope}}, which doesn’t exist on this computer
skip.pack_missing: Preset pack {{pack}}: this version of RRSS doesn’t include that pack
skip.memory_scope_missing: Memory “{{content}}”: limited to {{scope}}, which doesn’t exist on this computer

export.title: Export diagnostics
export.confirm:
Saves a ZIP file with recent logs (redacted again on export), plus version, system, and status details.
No database, settings, or keys. You choose where to save it, and whether to share it.

diagLog.title: Logs
diagLog.hint: Saved on this computer; old logs are cleaned up automatically.

other_instance.title: Another RRSS window is logging
other_instance.text: This window doesn’t write a log file. Close the other window and restart RRSS to resume logging.

not_writable.title: Can’t write to the log folder
not_writable.text: Check the permissions on the log folder, then restart RRSS.

disk_full.title: Not enough disk space; logging has stopped
disk_full.text: Free up disk space and restart RRSS, or clear the logs on the Storage page.

unclean.title: RRSS didn’t exit normally last time
unclean.bodyAt: Last logged {{when}}. You can export diagnostics to help find out why it exited.
unclean.body: You can export diagnostics to help find out why it exited.

level.label: Log level
level.detailedHint: Logs more troubleshooting detail and increases log size. Returns to Default after a restart.
level.defaultHint: Logs a summary of the run and any errors. Applies only until RRSS restarts.

feedback.label: Report a problem
feedback.hint: Export recent logs and status; attaching them to your report makes problems easier to pin down.

diag.loadFailed: Couldn’t load diagnostics: {{message}}. Refresh the status to try again.
diag.refreshFailed: Diagnostics couldn’t refresh, so the previous content is still shown; maintenance has run, so just refresh the status:

status.title: Status
status.hint: An overview of current data and usage. Click Refresh status to load it again.

embed.label: Generate article embeddings
embed.hint: Adds embeddings to a batch of content that doesn’t have them yet, making related articles and search by meaning more accurate. Using a remote model incurs charges.

retry.label: Allow failed content to retry
retry.hint: Content that failed before goes back in the queue. No articles are deleted.
retry.done: Queued again; these items will be processed later.

preview.stats: Sample data only; no local data loaded
preview.db: Not connected to the local database

subscribe.label: Feeds
subscribe.title: Feeds
subscribe.desc: Add sources, or import an existing list.

web.label: Web reading
web.title: Web reading
web.desc: How web links open, and which prompts appear.

rules.label: Rules
rules.title: Rules
rules.desc: Matching articles gain or lose points. Interests only affect ranking and aren’t changed here.

memory.label: Memories
memory.title: Memories
memory.desc: Preferences stored on this computer. Interests only affect ranking and never change rules.

model.label: Models
model.title: Models
model.desc: Pick a connection and model for each task. Tasks without a choice are paused.

assistant.label: Assistant
assistant.title: Assistant
assistant.desc: Which model chat uses, and what it can call.

translate.label: Translation
translate.title: Translation
translate.desc: The service is only called when you click “Translate” while reading; the original text isn’t rewritten.

diagnostics.label: Diagnostics
diagnostics.title: Status and troubleshooting
diagnostics.desc: Check how things are running and do maintenance when needed.

storage.label: Storage
storage.title: Storage
storage.desc: Cleanup only removes caches, never feeds or rules.

advanced.label: Advanced
advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.desc: You usually don’t need to change anything here. If models or the assistant misbehave, check the status at the top of the Assistant page first.

proxy.title: Network proxy
proxy.hint: Articles, model services, and the chat engine can each use their own connection. You usually don’t need to change this.
proxy.saved: Saved. New requests use this right away; an open chat uses the new settings only after the chat engine starts again.

global.name: Global
global.hint: All three tasks below use this setting unless they have their own.

content.name: Content network
content.hint: Feeds, full text, images, site icons, media, and web page reading.

api.name: Model API
api.hint: Summaries, digests, embeddings, translations, model lists, and connection tests.

pi.name: Pi
pi.hint: Downloading, updating, and chatting with the chat engine.

validate.incompleteUrl: Enter a complete proxy address, such as http://127.0.0.1:7890.
validate.noProxyFormat: The no-proxy list should contain only domains, IPs, network ranges, or *.

scheme.socks5h: SOCKS5H: the proxy resolves the target domain.
scheme.socks5: SOCKS5: this computer resolves the target domain; use socks5h:// to let the proxy do it.
scheme.default: Supports http, https, socks5, and socks5h; socks5h:// is recommended so the proxy resolves domains.

custom.noProxyHint: Domains, IPs, or network ranges separated by commas or spaces; * means connect directly. Local addresses always connect directly; add a range here for your LAN.

auth.title: Proxy authentication
auth.endpointChanged: The proxy scheme, host, or port has changed. To avoid sending saved credentials to a different proxy, the saved credentials will be cleared when you save. Enter new credentials if needed.
auth.hint: Not shown again after saving. Pasting an address with credentials moves them into these two fields automatically.

system.title: Detected system proxy
system.none: No proxy settings were found, so this mode connects directly.
system.pac: The system also has an auto-config script (PAC). RRSS doesn’t use it and connects using the address above.

check.title: Connection check
check.hint: Visits GitHub with the values currently entered, including unsaved changes; nothing is saved after the test.
check.socksNote: Whether chats can use a SOCKS proxy depends on the chat engine and model service; article and image downloads always support it.
check.httpTitle: Connected to GitHub, but it returned HTTP {{status}}

web_javascript.label: Allow JavaScript on original pages
web_javascript.hint: Applies to original pages opened after the change.

web_open_mode.label: Clicking external links
web_open_mode.hint: Right-click a link to choose another way at any time.

options.reader: Open in the RRSS reader view

web_first_tip.label: Remind you not to trust pages when opening

allow_embedding_model_change.label: Allow changing the embeddings model
allow_embedding_model_change.hint: Changing it rebuilds the entire vector store.

feed_icons_enabled.label: Show site icons
feed_icons_enabled.hint: Icons are saved locally; turning this off stops new downloads.

feed_fetch_per_host.label: Simultaneous downloads per site
feed_fetch_per_host.hint: How many feeds from the same site download at once. Raising it refreshes many feeds from one site faster (such as a self-hosted RSSHub), but may get rate-limited; a rate-limited site pauses for a while.
feed_fetch_per_host.control: Feeds downloaded at once per site (1–8)

ui_debug_mode.label: UI debug mode
ui_debug_mode.hint: Shows reader translation progress, pinned below the toolbar. Off by default.

ai_daily_budget_tokens.label: Daily generation budget
ai_daily_budget_tokens.hint: Background generation tasks such as auto-summary and auto-digest use at most this many tokens a day; they pause when it runs out and resume the next day. Manual article summaries and manual digests count toward usage but aren’t limited. 0 means no limit.
ai_daily_budget_tokens.control: Daily generation budget (10k tokens, 0 = no limit)

ai_embed_daily_budget_tokens.label: Daily embedding budget
ai_embed_daily_budget_tokens.hint: Counts embedding requests only (the vectors used for related articles, interests, and memory search). Running out stops embeddings only; summaries and digests keep working. Embedding on demand is also limited by it. 0 means no limit.
ai_embed_daily_budget_tokens.control: Daily embedding budget (10k tokens, 0 = no limit)

focus_summary_neutral_limit.label: Extra neutral unread summaries
focus_summary_neutral_limit.hint: Beyond high-scoring articles, also summarize this many neutral unread articles. This too looks only at recently added articles and counts toward the daily auto-summary limit. 0 turns it off.

ai_input_tier.label: Body text sent to the model
ai_input_tier.hint: Switching affects only summaries and digests generated afterward; existing summaries aren’t regenerated.

digest_generate_minutes.label: Auto-generate
digest_generate_minutes.hint: The daily digest is generated after this time each day; the weekly on Mondays after this time. If the app is closed, it catches up when you next open it. “Generate this digest” in the digest still works at any time.

pi_idle_timeout_secs.label: Release after idle (minutes)
pi_idle_timeout_secs.hint: After this long without a chat, the chat engine closes and frees memory; it starts again on the next message. 0 never releases it.

pi_assistant_note.label: Notes for the assistant
pi_assistant_note.hint: Included in every chat; good for preferences such as reply style or preferred language.

pi_auto_download.label: Auto-download
pi_auto_download.hint: Allow the app to download the chat engine automatically when it’s missing.

pi_auto_update.label: Auto-update
pi_auto_update.hint: Updates the chat engine within the versions the app supports.

close_action.label: When closing the window
close_action.hint: While hidden in the system tray, RRSS keeps updating feeds on schedule; click the tray icon or open RRSS again to come back.

pi_cache_warming.label: Cache warming
pi_cache_warming.hint: Keeping the provider’s prompt cache warm outside chats makes the next reply faster and cheaper, but costs extra.

optionHints.streaming: Keep the provider’s prompt cache warm while a reply streams.
optionHints.idle: Also keep it warm between questions; this may incur charges even with no chat open.

storage.loadFailed: Couldn’t measure storage use: {{message}}. Select Rescan to try again.
storage.rescanFailed: Rescan failed; still showing the last result. Select Rescan; there’s no need to clean again:

composition.hint: Hover over a bar or legend item to see each part’s size

total.title: Total
total.hintReady: Database, media cache, chat engine, and automatic backups combined.
total.hintScanning: Measuring reads through the database; a large library may take a few seconds, and you can keep using the app meanwhile.

messages.storage_auto_backups_other: {{count}} backups · Only the latest {{keep}} are kept
